claims.description: A black-box reconstruction model was developed using the observed query and score data. The objective was to approximate the hidden GK-05 scoring behavior from the available input features.

evidence.summary: The observed scores generally decrease as history_score increases across comparable queries, indicating a negative relationship between history_score and the GK-05 score.
The observed results indicate that higher requested_zone values are generally associated with lower GK-05 scores, with the effect becoming more noticeable at larger zone values.

Changing the site while keeping the other major inputs comparable produces substantially different GK-05 scores, indicating that site is an important categorical feature in the reconstructed behavior.
The observed scores show a tendency to decrease as linked_badges increases, suggesting a negative contribution from this feature.
The comparison between queries with different recent_denials values indicates that additional recent denials are associated with a lower GK-05 score.
Increasing badge_age_days in the observed comparison results in a lower GK-05 score, suggesting a moderate negative relationship.
The available observations do not provide sufficiently consistent evidence to establish a strong independent effect of escorts on the GK-05 score.

claims.description: The reconstruction uses the input features to estimate the continuous GK-05 score. Categorical site information is represented separately so that differences between sites can be captured by the model.

The exact hidden decision threshold could not be uniquely determined from the available observations. The reconstructed score should therefore be treated as an approximation of the black-box decision behavior.

The exact scoring formula, feature interactions, and behavior outside the observed input ranges remain uncertain. The reconstruction represents the behavior supported by the available query-response observations.
